mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without any regime dependency.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising PAYEMS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that typically boosts consumer confidence and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.0, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and negative quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an imminent monetary policy response to economic slowdown, which typically triggers positive equity market reaction as investors anticipate stimulus, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls > 0.25pp and GDPC1 growth rate (q/q) < 0
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS falls > 0.25pp and GDPC1 growth rate (q/q) < 0, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5pp over 3 months), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates applied to equity valuations.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp over 3 months, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1600 thousand units, it signals robust consumer demand for housing and related sectors, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1600, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals an imminent supply shock that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to recessionary concerns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls > 0.5% (m/m), the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days without any regime dependency.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods of rising RSAFS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher borrowing costs and reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.0, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
